## Text Normalization

Here we map:
- **URLs** to `[URL]` (`http(s)`, `www`, protocol-relative `//...`, then scheme-less `domain.tld/...`),
- **email-like** substrings to `[EMAIL]`,
- **@mentions** to `[USER]`,
- `mbc20` requests to `[MBC20]`

Whitespace is collapsed before substitution.

This stage runs in **Apache Spark** (local mode): read Parquet -> normalize -> derive optional word-count tables -> write
Parquet outputs. A **Java 8+** runtime must be available on `PATH`. On smaller machines, JVM startup overhead can be
noticeable; Spark becomes more beneficial as data size grows.

## Operation Order

The pipeline applies the following order of operations:

1. Load data, first trying `*-norm.parquet` to resume from existing normalized text.
2. If normalized tables are not available, load `*-clean.parquet` and create `normalized` text:
   URL/email/mention/mbc20 replacement + whitespace collapse.
3. Build original and normalized dictionaries (posts/comments).
4. Build `preprocessed` text from `normalized`:
   uncontract -> remove quoted lines (`>`/`|>`) -> lowercase -> remove punctuation/digit-only tokens -> remove stopwords.
5. Build preprocessed dictionaries.
6. From preprocessed text, build stemmed dictionaries and lemmatized dictionaries (separate branches).
7. Save row-level tables (`norm`, `preprocessed`) and dictionary tables (`norm-bow`, `preprocessed-bow`,
   `preprocessed-stemmed-bow`, `preprocessed-lemmatized-bow`).

```{python}
#| label: preprocess-spark-pipeline
#| message: false

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import StringType

from utils import SparkData, DATA_DIR

# Java regex patterns (same order as the old pandas pipeline). (?i) / (?is) = case / dotall.
_RE_EMAIL = r"(?i)\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"
_RE_MBC20 = r'(?is)\{\s*"p"\s*:\s*"mbc-20".*?\}'
_RE_BARE = (
    r"(?i)\b(?!www\.)(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}(?:/[^\s\[\]<>]*)+"
)


def _normalize_spark_column(c: F.Column) -> F.Column:
    x = F.trim(F.coalesce(c.cast("string"), F.lit("")))
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, r"\s+", " ")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, r"(?i)https?://\S+", "[URL]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, r"(?i)\bwww\.\S+", "[URL]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, r"(?i)(?<![:/])//\S+", "[URL]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, _RE_EMAIL, "[EMAIL]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, _RE_BARE, "[URL]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, r"(?i)(?<![\w])@\w+", "[USER]")
    x = F.regexp_replace(x, _RE_MBC20, "[MBC20]")
    return x


def _word_count_col(c: F.Column) -> F.Column:
    t = F.trim(F.coalesce(c, F.lit("")))
    return F.when(F.length(t) == 0, F.lit(0)).otherwise(F.size(F.split(t, " ")))


def make_dictionary_spark(sdf: DataFrame, text_col: str) -> DataFrame:
    """Whitespace-split word counts pooled across all rows (descending by count)."""
    col = F.trim(F.coalesce(F.col(text_col), F.lit("")))
    words = sdf.select(F.explode(F.split(col, r"\s+")).alias("word"))
    words = words.filter(F.length(F.col("word")) > 0)
    return words.groupBy("word").count().orderBy(F.desc("count"), F.col("word"))


def _uncontract_text(text: str) -> str:
    text = re.sub(
        r"(\b)([Aa]re|[Cc]ould|[Dd]id|[Dd]oes|[Dd]o|[Hh]ad|[Hh]as|[Hh]ave|[Ii]s|[Mm]ight|[Mm]ust|[Ss]hould|[Ww]ere|[Ww]ould)n't",
        r"\1\2 not",
        text,
    )
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Hh]e|[Ii]|[Ss]he|[Tt]hey|[Ww]e|[Ww]hat|[Ww]ho|[Yy]ou)'ll", r"\1\2 will", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Tt]hey|[Ww]e|[Ww]hat|[Ww]ho|[Yy]ou)'re", r"\1\2 are", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Ii]|[Ss]hould|[Tt]hey|[Ww]e|[Ww]hat|[Ww]ho|[Ww]ould|[Yy]ou)'ve", r"\1\2 have", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Cc]a)n't", r"\1\2n not", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Ii])'m", r"\1\2 am", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Ll]et)'s", r"\1\2 us", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Tt]here)'s", r"\1\2 is", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Ww])on't", r"\1\2ill not", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Ss])han't", r"\1\2hall not", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(\b)([Yy])(?:'all|a'll)", r"\1\2ou all", text)
    return text


def _is_punct_or_digit_token(token: str) -> bool:
    return bool(token) and all(ch.isdigit() or ch in string.punctuation for ch in token)


def _preprocess_text(text: str | None) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return ""
    x = str(text)
    x = _uncontract_text(x)
    x = re.sub(r"^>.*(?:\n|$)|\|>.*(?:\n|$)", "", x, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    x = x.lower()
    tokens = [t for t in re.split(r"\s+", x.strip()) if t]
    tokens = [t for t in tokens if not _is_punct_or_digit_token(t)]
    tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in _STOPWORDS]
    return " ".join(tokens)


def _stem_text(text: str | None) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return ""
    tokens = [t for t in str(text).split() if t]
    return " ".join(_STEMMER.stem(t) for t in tokens)


def _lemmatize_text(text: str | None) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return ""
    tokens = [t for t in str(text).split() if t]
    return " ".join(_LEMMATIZER.lemmatize(t) for t in tokens)


spark = (
    SparkSession.builder.appName("moltbook-preprocess")
    .master("local[4]")
    .config("spark.driver.memory", "4g")
    .config("spark.executor.memory", "4g")
    .config("spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled", "true")
    .config("spark.sql.legacy.parquet.nanosAsLong", "true")
    .config("spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader", "false")
    .config("spark.hadoop.parquet.read.vectored.io.enabled", "false")
    .config("spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes", str(16 * 1024 * 1024))
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "8")
    .config("spark.ui.showConsoleProgress", "false")
    .getOrCreate()
)
spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")

import re
import string

import nltk
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from nltk.stem import PorterStemmer, WordNetLemmatizer

nltk.download("wordnet", quiet=True)
nltk.download("omw-1.4", quiet=True)
nltk.download("stopwords", quiet=True)
_STEMMER = PorterStemmer()
_LEMMATIZER = WordNetLemmatizer()
_STOPWORDS = set(stopwords.words("english"))

preprocess_udf = F.udf(_preprocess_text, StringType())
stem_udf = F.udf(_stem_text, StringType())
lemma_udf = F.udf(_lemmatize_text, StringType())

def _has_column(sdf: DataFrame | None, col: str) -> bool:
    return sdf is not None and col in sdf.columns


data = SparkData(spark).load("norm")
posts = data.posts
comments = data.comments

if _has_column(posts, "normalized") and (comments is None or _has_column(comments, "normalized")):
    print("Loaded existing normalized parquet (resume mode).")
else:
    print("Normalized parquet missing/incomplete; rebuilding from clean tables.")
    data = SparkData(spark).load("clean")
    posts = data.posts
    posts = (
        posts.withColumn("normalized", _normalize_spark_column(F.col("post")))
        .withColumn("post_length", F.length(F.col("normalized")))
        .withColumn("word_count", _word_count_col(F.col("normalized")))
    )
    print("Prepared normalized posts column")
    data.posts = posts

    comments = data.comments
    if comments is not None:
        comments = (
            comments.withColumn("normalized", _normalize_spark_column(F.col("content")))
            .withColumn("post_length", F.length(F.col("normalized")))
            .withColumn("word_count", _word_count_col(F.col("normalized")))
        )
        print("Prepared normalized comments column")
    data.comments = comments
    data.save("norm")

original_posts_df = make_dictionary_spark(posts, "post")
normalized_posts_df = make_dictionary_spark(posts, "normalized")

if comments is not None:
    original_comments_df = make_dictionary_spark(comments, "content")
    normalized_comments_df = make_dictionary_spark(comments, "normalized")
else:
    original_comments_df = None
    normalized_comments_df = None

posts_preprocessed = (
    posts.withColumn("preprocessed", preprocess_udf(F.col("normalized")))
    .withColumn("preprocessed_word_count", _word_count_col(F.col("preprocessed")))
)
print("Prepared posts preprocessed column")

if comments is not None:
    comments_preprocessed = (
        comments.withColumn("preprocessed", preprocess_udf(F.col("normalized")))
        .withColumn("preprocessed_word_count", _word_count_col(F.col("preprocessed")))
    )
    print("Prepared comments preprocessed column")
else:
    comments_preprocessed = None

preprocessed_posts_df = make_dictionary_spark(posts_preprocessed, "preprocessed")
preprocessed_comments_df = (
    make_dictionary_spark(comments_preprocessed, "preprocessed")
    if comments_preprocessed is not None
    else None
)

stemmed_posts_df = make_dictionary_spark(
    posts_preprocessed.withColumn("preprocessed_stemmed", stem_udf(F.col("preprocessed"))),
    "preprocessed_stemmed",
)
stemmed_comments_df = (
    make_dictionary_spark(
        comments_preprocessed.withColumn("preprocessed_stemmed", stem_udf(F.col("preprocessed"))),
        "preprocessed_stemmed",
    )
    if comments_preprocessed is not None
    else None
)

lemmatized_posts_df = make_dictionary_spark(
    posts_preprocessed.withColumn("preprocessed_lemmatized", lemma_udf(F.col("preprocessed"))),
    "preprocessed_lemmatized",
)
lemmatized_comments_df = (
    make_dictionary_spark(
        comments_preprocessed.withColumn("preprocessed_lemmatized", lemma_udf(F.col("preprocessed"))),
        "preprocessed_lemmatized",
    )
    if comments_preprocessed is not None
    else None
)

data_preprocessed = SparkData(spark, agents=data.agents, submolts=data.submolts)
data_preprocessed.posts = posts_preprocessed
data_preprocessed.comments = comments_preprocessed
data_preprocessed.save("preprocessed")

SparkData(
    spark,
    posts=normalized_posts_df,
    comments=normalized_comments_df,
).save("norm-bow")

SparkData(
    spark,
    posts=preprocessed_posts_df,
    comments=preprocessed_comments_df,
).save("preprocessed-bow")

SparkData(
    spark,
    posts=stemmed_posts_df,
    comments=stemmed_comments_df,
).save("preprocessed-stemmed-bow")

SparkData(
    spark,
    posts=lemmatized_posts_df,
    comments=lemmatized_comments_df,
).save("preprocessed-lemmatized-bow")
```

```{python}
#| label: preprocess-dictionary-plots
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Token-frequency distributions and placeholder-token counts in normalized text.
#| message: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display


def _to_rank_df(sdf, top_n: int = 5000) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    if sdf is None:
        return None
    pdf = sdf.select("word", "count").limit(top_n).toPandas()
    if pdf.empty:
        return None
    pdf["rank"] = range(1, len(pdf) + 1)
    return pdf


rank_posts_orig = _to_rank_df(original_posts_df)
rank_posts_norm = _to_rank_df(normalized_posts_df)
rank_comments_orig = _to_rank_df(original_comments_df) if original_comments_df is not None else None
rank_comments_norm = _to_rank_df(normalized_comments_df) if normalized_comments_df is not None else None

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

# Posts distribution
ax = axes[0]
if rank_posts_orig is not None:
    ax.loglog(rank_posts_orig["rank"], rank_posts_orig["count"], label="Original posts", alpha=0.85)
if rank_posts_norm is not None:
    ax.loglog(rank_posts_norm["rank"], rank_posts_norm["count"], label="Normalized posts", alpha=0.85)
ax.set(
    title="Posts Dictionary Distribution (Rank vs Count)",
    xlabel="Token rank",
    ylabel="Token frequency",
)
ax.legend()

# Comments distribution
ax = axes[1]
if rank_comments_orig is not None:
    ax.loglog(rank_comments_orig["rank"], rank_comments_orig["count"], label="Original comments", alpha=0.85)
if rank_comments_norm is not None:
    ax.loglog(rank_comments_norm["rank"], rank_comments_norm["count"], label="Normalized comments", alpha=0.85)
ax.set(
    title="Comments Dictionary Distribution (Rank vs Count)",
    xlabel="Token rank",
    ylabel="Token frequency",
)
if rank_comments_orig is not None or rank_comments_norm is not None:
    ax.legend()

fig.tight_layout()


placeholders = ["[URL]", "[EMAIL]", "[USER]", "[MBC20]"]

def _placeholder_counts(sdf) -> pd.Series:
    if sdf is None:
        return pd.Series([0] * len(placeholders), index=placeholders, dtype="int64")
    pdf = (
        sdf.filter(sdf.word.isin(placeholders))
        .toPandas()
        .set_index("word")["count"]
        if sdf is not None
        else pd.Series(dtype="int64")
    )
    return pdf.reindex(placeholders, fill_value=0)


ph_posts = _placeholder_counts(normalized_posts_df)
ph_comments = _placeholder_counts(normalized_comments_df) if normalized_comments_df is not None else pd.Series(
    [0] * len(placeholders), index=placeholders, dtype="int64"
)

ph_df = pd.DataFrame({"Posts": ph_posts, "Comments": ph_comments})
ax = ph_df.plot.bar(
    figsize=(10, 5),
    rot=0,
    color=["steelblue", "coral"],
    title="Placeholder Tokens in Normalized Dictionaries",
    xlabel="Placeholder token",
    ylabel="Count",
)
ax.legend(title="Source")
ax.figure.tight_layout()

placeholder_table = ph_df.copy()
placeholder_table["Total"] = placeholder_table["Posts"] + placeholder_table["Comments"]
display(placeholder_table.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "token"}))
```

The post dictionary rank-frequency curve follows a heavy-tailed (Zipf-like) pattern: a small set of very frequent
tokens dominates, while most tokens appear relatively rarely. Comparing original vs normalized posts shows how
normalization consolidates noisy lexical variants into shared placeholders such as `[URL]` and `[USER]`.

```{python}
#| label: preprocess-normalized-wordclouds
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Wordclouds of preprocessed dictionaries for posts and comments.
#| message: false

from wordcloud import WordCloud


def _to_freq_dict(sdf, top_n: int = 5000) -> dict[str, int]:
    if sdf is None:
        return {}
    pdf = sdf.select("word", "count").limit(top_n).toPandas()
    return dict(zip(pdf["word"], pdf["count"].astype(int)))


posts_freq = _to_freq_dict(preprocessed_posts_df)
comments_freq = _to_freq_dict(preprocessed_comments_df) if preprocessed_comments_df is not None else {}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

if posts_freq:
    wc_posts = WordCloud(width=900, height=500, background_color="white", colormap="Blues").generate_from_frequencies(posts_freq)
    axes[0].imshow(wc_posts, interpolation="bilinear")
axes[0].set(title="Preprocessed Posts Dictionary Wordcloud")
axes[0].axis("off")

if comments_freq:
    wc_comments = WordCloud(width=900, height=500, background_color="white", colormap="Oranges").generate_from_frequencies(comments_freq)
    axes[1].imshow(wc_comments, interpolation="bilinear")
axes[1].set(title="Preprocessed Comments Dictionary Wordcloud")
axes[1].axis("off")

fig.tight_layout()
```

```{python}
def _display_top_bottom_tokens(sdf, label: str) -> None:
    if sdf is None:
        return
    top = sdf.orderBy(F.desc("count"), F.asc("word")).limit(10).toPandas()
    bottom = sdf.orderBy(F.asc("count"), F.asc("word")).limit(10).toPandas()
    print(f"{label} - Top 10 tokens")
    display(top)
    print(f"{label} - Bottom 10 tokens")
    display(bottom)


_display_top_bottom_tokens(preprocessed_posts_df, "Preprocessed posts dictionary")
_display_top_bottom_tokens(preprocessed_comments_df, "Preprocessed comments dictionary")
```
